reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in constructing a reproducible pipeline from raw play-by-play data to player-level impact metrics. The expected points estimator uses multinomial logistic regression to map game states to probabilistic point outcomes, enabling quantification of strategic value per play. This is then fed into a generalized additive model to compute win probabilities dynamically over time, capturing temporal dependencies in game dynamics. Finally, the multilevel model isolates individual player contributions by comparing conditional win probabilities with and without specific players, yielding a WAR metric. Each step builds upon previous ones, forming a coherent chain of inference grounded in public data and statistical rigor. Failure modes include overfitting in small sample sizes, misclassification of game states, and lack of accurate replacement benchmarks. These are mitigated through cross-validation, robust modeling techniques, and resampling-based uncertainty quantification.
